BACKPORT: FROMGIT: spi: Allow SPI devices to request the pumping thread be realtime Right now the only way to get the SPI pumping thread bumped up to realtime priority is for the controller to request it. However it may be that the controller works fine with the normal priority but communication to a particular SPI device on the bus needs realtime priority. Let's add a way for devices to request realtime priority when they set themselves up. NOTE: this will just affect the priority of transfers that end up on the SPI core's pumping thread. In many cases transfers happen in the context of the caller so if you need realtime priority for all transfers you should ensure the calling context is also realtime priority. Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> Tested-by: Enric Balletbo i Serra <enric.balletbo@collabora.com> Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org> (cherry picked from commit 924b5867e7bd6a6a98014f0517b747465b108011 git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/broonie/spi.git topic/pump-rt) Conflicts: include/linux/spi/spi.h ...context: "mode" is u16 in our tree and u32 upstream. FROMLIST: platform/chrome: cros_ec_spi: Request the SPI thread be realtime All currently known ECs in the wild are very sensitive to timing. Specifically the ECs are known to drop a transfer if more than 8 ms passes from the assertion of the chip select until the transfer finishes. Let's use the new feature introduced in the patch (spi: Allow SPI devices to request the pumping thread be realtime") to request the SPI pumping thread be realtime. This means that if we get shunted off to the SPI thread for whatever reason we won't get downgraded to low priority. NOTES: - We still need to keep ourselves as high priority since the SPI core doesn't guarantee that all transfers end up on the pumping thread (in fact, it tries pretty hard to do them in the calling context). - If future Chrome OS ECs ever fix themselves to be less sensitive then we could consider adding a property (or compatible string) to not set this property. For now we need it across the board. biod: Add more unit tests for cros_fp_firmware These unit tests cover all code paths in cros_fp_firmware.cc, other than the error handing for image_fmap_aligned Initialize and the kUninitialized case of GetStatusString. It should be noted that we do not test extremely malformed firmware files, like a file that only contains a fake FMAP signature. This is because the underlying fmap library is not capable of gracefully handling these malicious cases. chromeos-base/arc-keymaster: Setup libhardware and shared libs Use libhardware headers from arc-toolchain-p and install shared libraries in the system. Keymaster depends on libhardware, which is part of the arc toolchain. We can't inherit from arc-build because we don't want the full toolchain. This builds a CrOS daemon, and the toolchain conflicts with the CrOS build tools. Instead we copy the relevant headers from libhardware to WORKDIR. We use arc-toolchain-p specifically because this package doesn't support ARC N, and we can rely on the keymaster backwards compatibility layer for this to work on P and newer ARC versions. BUG=b:110136496 TEST=emerge-eve chromeos-base/arc-keymaster Change-Id: I2654f19f8a941a862c93b18c23dcc0478c36d54a Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1477239 Commit-Ready: Edman Anjos <edman@chromium.org> Tested-by: Edman Anjos <edman@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>

shill: drop ad-hoc support Ad-hoc networks are * used at a negligible rate; * known to be broken, to some extent (e.g., we disconnect/reconnect during every scan); * not supported by all vendors; and * not tested in our automated lab. Let's drop support for them. For the moment, I leave the 'Mode' Service property intact, even though it only serves to advertise a single option now ('managed'). We stop reporting metrics -- will follow up with removal of the histogram in Chrome. Notable behaviors: * we now filter out any unsupported mode when reporting endpoints (WiFi::BSSAddedTask()), which prevents ad-hoc networks from showing up in our Service list; this gets tested now in WiFiMainTest.ScanResults * we *don't* explicitly purge old stored Profile entries which could still have WiFi.Mode==adhoc; these will get loaded, but they won't do anything if no endpoint is matched to them BUG=chromium:931442 TEST=unit tests TEST=manual: set up IBSS network -- does not appear in Service list Change-Id: Ib4db4f54d171e767a8af8440f45ac23573563b70 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1626253 Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org>

Connect a Headset that supports Codec negotiation and MSBC support. Alt6 setting shall be used for the connection.
